subject: Post-demo throughput gates & token velocity next steps
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Kai Nakamura <kai@ledgerai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T15:23:00Z
Subject: Post-demo throughput gates & token velocity next steps

Hi Kai — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we have a single source of truth: 

Summary from call
- Use case: document ingestion + context-aware summarization for customer support (mix of short/long interactions).
- Integration mode: streaming response for chat UI (server-side streaming), occasional batch jobs for nightly enrichment.

Numbers you gave (please confirm):
- Baseline sustained QPS: ~60 requests/sec
- Peak bursts: up to ~600 requests/sec (typical crest windows ~2–5 minutes)
- Avg tokens per request: 900 tokens (range 200–2,400)
- Expected 99th P-token latency target (streaming end-to-end): P99 < 1.2s per token emission, overall P99 for first reply < 1.5s
- Concurrent streams per session: ~2 (concurrent connections per end-user)

Asks / data requests (action items)
1) Please confirm true peak tokens/sec during crest windows (tokens/sec = tokens/request * QPS). If you have a 1-hour sample or CSV, attach it.
2) Any hard retention or audit log windows (e.g., 7/30/90 days) and whether logs must remain in your VPC.
3) Confirm if fallbacks are acceptable (e.g., lower-capacity quantized model when Dedicated pool saturated).
4) Any IP allowlists / cloud region constraints (we noted US-east preferred).

Attached: ledgerai_workload_snapshot.csv — sample 72h ingestion summary (columns: ts, qps, tokens_per_req_mean, median_latency_ms).

Next steps proposed
- You share the confirmed token/sec crest numbers + any sample payloads (by EOD Thurs).
- We run an internal feasibility sweep (Marissa) and return a capacity sketch + recommended pilot size by Fri.
- Schedule 60-min technical deep-dive to validate streaming SLOs and latency tracing (suggest Mon or Tue next week).

Happy to hop on quick sync if any of this is off.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
[attachment: ledgerai_workload_snapshot.csv (csv)]

From: Kai Nakamura <kai@ledgerai.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+pilot@ledgerai.com
Date: 2026-10-23T09:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo throughput gates & token velocity next steps

Hey Monica — thanks for the clear recap, looks good. Quick clarifications and an extra file attached.

Corrections / confirmations:
- Sustained QPS: expected 50–70 (we typically operate around 60 globally; first 45 days pilot traffic may be lower).
- Peak bursts: more like 8–10x baseline for marketing-driven spikes; our worst-case crest observed last quarter was ~650 QPS for ~3 minutes.
- Tokens/request: average 900 is accurate; during some multi-doc sessions it can hit 2,400.
- Streaming behavior: yes, server-side streaming. We need consistent per-token pacing (clients depend on partial outputs).
- Concurrency: about 1.5 active streams per user on average; plan for 3 concurrent connections per account as a cushion.

Attached: ledgerai_latency_requirements.docx — contains internal latency SLAs and a short compliance checklist. Also note: we run all customer PII obfuscation on our side; Redwood will see pre-processed text.

Retention: we need 30 days of request traces in your control plane logs for the pilot; final production may need 90 days (will confirm).

We can accept fallback to a slightly quantized model for non-topline traffic as long as summary quality delta is within agreed evaluation thresholds.

I can do the tech-deep-dive Tue 10/27 15:00 ET or Wed 10/28 11:00 ET — 60 minutes. Which works for you?

-Kai
Kai Nakamura
Head of Platform — LedgerAI
[kai@ledgerai.com]
[attachment: ledgerai_latency_requirements.docx (docx)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-23T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo throughput gates & token velocity next steps

Copying my estimates here based on Kai's numbers — I will run a short capacity sketch tomorrow morning:
- Baseline: 60 QPS * 900 tokens = 54k tokens/sec sustained.
- Peak crest: 650 QPS * 2,400 tokens (worst-case) = 1.56M tokens/sec (extreme; we'll treat as stress test).
- Realistic planning window: design for 10x baseline burst headroom (so ~600 QPS; median tokens ~900 -> ~540k tokens/sec).
- Streaming: prioritize low P99 token emission latency; we should budget smaller batch sizes and conservative KV cache sizing for streaming workloads.

I’ll produce a couple runner-up configs (Dedicated pool sizing + a fallback quantized model profile) and drop them to the HubSpot ticket and shared drive.

Also, Monica — Tue 10/27 15:00 ET works; I'll join the deep-dive.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Performance Engineering — Redwood Inference
